title: Microsoft exec called AI scraping ‘the largest theft of labor in human history,’ new unredacted filings reveal
slides: Microsoft called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor'?
Unredacted filings reveal executive's stark warning.
Yet Microsoft's own AI uses scraped data.
If your work is online, it may be training AI.
Check if your content is in public datasets.
thread_text:
1. Microsoft's Theft Warning

Microsoft called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor' in unredacted filings. But the same company's AI reportedly uses scraped data. That contradiction is the story.

2. The Hidden Hypocrisy

Internal documents show an executive warned about the practice, yet the company continued. The warning was buried until now.

3. Your Work Is The Fuel

If you've published anything online, it may already be in a training dataset. No permission required.

4. Check If You're Included

Public datasets like Books3 and LAION were built from web scraping. You can search some of them directly.

5. Take Action Today

Search your name or domain in Dataset Search. If you find it, you know where you stand. Do it now.
